text.p: India's state-run international telecommunications provider, Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) said on Wednesday that it had entered a period of high growth after its successful $526.6 million stock floatation.

"We have invested all that we had promised to invest at the time of the GDR issue. Our projects are going ahead as scheduled," B.K. Syngal, VSNL's chairman and managing director told Reuters in an interview.
He said that in three years time VSNL would have 25 international gateways, with 11 earthstations. He added that it would also be part of three international cable systems.

Syngal said that VSNL is adding five new earthstations to its existing ones. The new ones are coming up at Jullundur, Kanpur, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Kanpur. "We expect three to be ready by the end of 1997 and Kanpur and Hyderabad to follow suit next year."

On cable systems, he said that VSNL had invested in three systems, the first of which, FLAG (Fibre Optic Link Around the Globe) would start functioning in September. VSNL has invested $35 million in FLAG.
The other two systems, SEA-ME-WE (South East Asia-Middle East-West Asia) and OASIS (Optically Amplified Super Information System) were also on course, Syngal said.
Syngal said that VSNL was still to take a view on its proposal to offer direct-to-home (DTH) broadcast services.
"We are keen to use our Madras and Dehradun earthstations to start offering broadcasters uplink facilities, but the final shape of things will depend on the government's policy on DTH," he said.
He said VSNL had a consortium in place with the Indian Space Research Organisation and international satellite communications organisation, Inmarsat.

"We want to offer broadcasters the facility to uplink from India. We will just provide the technical platform. The content, marketing of the service and promotion will all be done by the broadcaster," Syngal said.
Syngal said that the investment in this project would be in the region of $200 million, but that would be split among the partners.

Speaking about the internet, he said that VSNL's subscriber base was expected to touch 100,000 by the end of the year. He added that it was about 40,000 now, and was growing at 10 to 12 percent a month.

VSNL earned a net profit of 5.03 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) as compared to 4.08 billion in 1995/96. Its revenues grew to 51.94 billion rupees in 1996/97 as compared to 44.343 billion rupees in the previous year.
International paid minutes increased to 1.38 billion in 1996/97 from 1.14 billion in the previous year, according to a statement issued by the company last month.
Syngal said that the company would go in for an expansion of its international lines in two to three months. He said VSNL would add 25,000 lines.
